knowledge.statement: An application FSM that implements both BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore never receives StoreConfiguration for a committed configuration change, even though ConfigurationStore documents that callback as invoked once a configuration change is committed. runFSM decides once whether the FSM implements BatchingFSM and then routes every applied batch through applyBatch; that path sends LogConfiguration entries to ApplyBatch and contains no StoreConfiguration call, while StoreConfiguration is only reached from applySingle, which runs when batching is disabled. Two executions of the same probe agree exactly: the dual-interface FSM recorded 0 StoreConfiguration calls and 6 ApplyBatch configuration entries after one committed configuration change, against 6 and 0 for the ConfigurationStore-only control.
knowledge.conditions: An FSM type whose method set satisfies both interfaces (BatchingFSM embeds FSM, ConfigurationStore embeds FSM); a committed configuration change, here an AddVoter that moved an existing voter's address in a three-voter cluster built with the repository's own helper, in-memory transports and stores.

interpretations.rationale: The question was whether an FSM implementing both BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore still receives StoreConfiguration for a committed configuration change, as that interface documents, or only through ApplyBatch. The execution answers that it receives only ApplyBatch: in the dual-interface case the recorder shows 0 StoreConfiguration calls and 6 ApplyBatch configuration entries (parsed result event 3), while the ConfigurationStore-only control shows 6 and 0 (result event 1), with the setup events (0 and 2) matched as admissions and every comparison resolving. The source gives the mechanism: runFSM computes batchingEnabled once, and once it is true every batch goes to applyBatch, which forwards LogCommand and LogConfiguration entries to ApplyBatch and never calls StoreConfiguration; StoreConfiguration is reached only from applySingle, which the batched path does not use. What makes this a defect rather than a naming preference is the purpose the interface states for itself: storing configuration changes so that a persistent FSM state can behave as a complete snapshot and recover without an external one. An application that implements ConfigurationStore for that purpose, and also batches its applies for throughput, gets no callback and no error, so its durable state silently lacks the configuration it was promised. The scope is bounded and I record it plainly: the same entries do reach ApplyBatch, which BatchingFSM documents as receiving LogConfiguration, so an implementation that handles configuration changes in both places loses nothing observable, and the defect is the silent failure of the documented callback rather than lost information. A repeat of the same fixed experiment reproduced both counts exactly (receipt a5809ed4b5024b17adfebf093d3316f5, result events at parsed indices 1 and 3): the dual-interface FSM recorded 0 StoreConfiguration calls and 6 ApplyBatch configuration entries, the ConfigurationStore-only control recorded 6 and 0, and all four comparisons resolved as before. The account therefore rests on two executions rather than one, and the counts being identical across them is what makes the zero credible rather than an artifact of a single run's timing.

knowledge.assertion: An FSM implementing both interfaces receives configuration changes only through ApplyBatch; two executions of the same probe recorded the same zero and six counts.

counterevidence: The configuration entry is not lost: BatchingFSM documents that ApplyBatch receives LogConfiguration entries, and the receipt shows all 6 deliveries there, so an application handling both paths is unaffected.

The combination is unusual rather than forbidden: nothing in either interface documents mutual exclusion, but an application that implements only one of them sees the documented behaviour, as the control case shows.
The trigger was a single configuration change (moving an existing voter's address); the same code path handles every LogConfiguration entry, but other change commands were not measured.
limitations: The interactions are measured in two executions of the same fixed probe, which agree exactly (dual-interface FSM 0 StoreConfiguration calls and 6 ApplyBatch configuration entries; control 6 and 0), but both use three-voter clusters built by the repository's own helper with a shared recorder.
The change was triggered through AddVoter with a new address for an existing voter, which is a legal change but not the AddNonvoter or RemoveServer paths.
